intuition.title: Two concentrations and two composition bases
intuition.text: The target is 8 mol% Sc2O3-stabilized zirconia on an oxide basis. The method separately prints nominal starting values of 92 mol% ZrO(NO3)2 and 16 mol% Sc(NO3)3. Those literal feed values are not two normalized percentages summing to 100, nor an 8 mol% scandium-cation fraction. Total cation concentration is separate from urea concentration. The stock solvent and individual nitrate charges are not specified.

intuition.title: Aging changes phase formation
intuition.text: The authors attribute the low-temperature stage to slow urea hydrolysis and homogeneous co-precipitation before crystallization at 180 °C. They propose polymeric/hydrous-oxide intermediates and a more ordered precursor; these are mechanistic interpretations, not measured transient species or molecular structures. Direct 180 °C treatment gives more monoclinic phase.
intuition.source_locator: Main PDF p. 2, Results and Discussion; Figure 2

intuition.title: The 0.5 mol/L boundary remains unresolved
intuition.text: The first-page discussion describes pure cubic material for urea ≤0.5 mol/L. The conclusion uses <0.5 mol/L, and Figure 2a shows a small nonzero monoclinic point at 0.5 mol/L. The 0.5 mol/L route therefore retains an unresolved phase-purity boundary rather than a blanket pure-cubic label or an invented exact fraction.
intuition.source_locator: Main PDF p. 1–3, Results, Figure 2a and Conclusions

intuition.title: The short concentration series is a separate schedule
intuition.text: Figure 3 uses 80 °C for 24 h followed by 180 °C for 48 h, at 0.05, 0.1, 0.25 and 0.5 mol/L total cations with cation:urea = 1:4. The long urea series uses 48 h followed by 72 h. The 0.5 mol/L cation endpoint with that ratio is not silently reconciled with the general 0.1–1.5 mol/L urea range. Individual phase fractions for Figure 3 are not tabulated.
intuition.source_locator: Main PDF p. 1–2, Experimental Procedure and Figure 3

intuition.title: Three size estimates describe different observables
intuition.text: For 0.05 mol/L cations and 0.2 mol/L urea after the long schedule, TEM gives an average grain size below 10 nm, XRD linewidth analysis gives 7.0 nm, and BET gives a specific surface area of 157 m²/g with an author-calculated equivalent size of 6 nm. These are separate analytical quantities, not repeated TEM diameters. Figure 5 shows a 50 nm scale bar.
intuition.source_locator: Main PDF p. 3, Figure 5 and morphology/XRD/BET paragraph

intuition.title: Calcination retains cubic phase while promoting grain growth
intuition.text: The paper reports cubic phase retention during 1 h calcination under stagnant air over 600–1200 °C. Grain size changes little below 800 °C and grows substantially above 1000 °C, reaching a text-reported XRD crystallite size of 36.5 nm at 1200 °C. Other Figure 6 point ordinates are preserved visually without extracting exact numbers.
intuition.source_locator: Main PDF p. 1, 3, Experimental Procedure, calcination paragraph and Figure 6

intuition.title: Solution pH and applications are separate scopes
intuition.text: Figure 4 shows increasing final solution pH and decreasing XRD crystallite size as urea concentration rises. The plotted pH and size ordinates are not tabulated here. The paper motivates solid-oxide fuel-cell electrolytes through cited literature but supplies no conductivity measurement for these powders.
intuition.source_locator: Main PDF p. 1–2, Introduction and Figure 4

general_background.title: Thermodynamics and kinetics
general_background.summary: Thermodynamics describes which states are energetically favoured, while kinetics governs how quickly a system can move between them. A change can be favourable yet proceed slowly when an activation barrier or limited transport restricts the pathway.
general_background.label: General background, not the authors' interpretation
